text: Light from a star that may no longer exist came through the port window again. The charts stayed rolled. I worked by hand, off the record. Out.

A meteor shower off the port bow, silent as a held breath. Logged 13 faults in [herdr-maroon](https://github.com/RKPinata/herdr-maroon). Answered a hail from [herdr-maroon](https://github.com/RKPinata/herdr-maroon). Logged a fault in [herdrdev/herdr-app](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-app). Signing off with the lights low.
Somewhere aft, a panel rattled. I have stopped asking which one. Answered no hails. Fixed three things that were not broken yet. End of entry.
The hull ticked as it cooled. Held position. Not every day is a jump. Fuel enough. Faith enough. Goodnight.
The radio gave us twenty minutes of static that sounded almost like rain. No new stars marked. I counted the old ones instead, to make sure they were still there. Bearing unchanged. Spirits fair.
Woke to the hum of the recyclers and a sky that had not moved. Kept the lights low and the hatches shut. Some work wants no audience. More tomorrow, if the stars stay where I left them.
The galley plants have started leaning toward the reading lamp. So have I. The open channels stayed quiet. Below deck, the engines ran anyway. Nothing further. The dark is patient.

A slow day by the ship’s clock, though the ship’s clock has opinions. Put in at [shell-scripts](https://github.com/RKPinata/shell-scripts) long enough to change one thing. Closing the book. The pen stays warm.
Dreamed of a harbour I have never seen. Woke with salt on my tongue. One commit to [shell-scripts](https://github.com/RKPinata/shell-scripts), small and clean. Logging off. The stars can keep watch.
The navigation lamp blinked green all night. I chose to read it as encouragement. A day for maintenance and long thoughts. Neither leaves a trace on the public band. Course holds.
The old map still shows a coastline here. I keep it pinned up anyway. Spent the watch below, mending things nobody will see. Out.
Frost on the inside of the viewport this morning. I drew a door in it. No public transmissions. The real work happened below deck, where the logs are sealed. Signing off with the lights low.
Nothing on the long-range scanners but the usual dust. The charts stayed rolled. I worked by hand, off the record. End of entry.
We crossed into the planet’s shadow and the cabin went blue for an hour. Nothing on the public frequencies. Some voyages are made in the dark. Fuel enough. Faith enough. Goodnight.
The coffee ration held. Small mercies. Answered no hails. Fixed three things that were not broken yet. Bearing unchanged. Spirits fair.
Ran the diagnostics twice. Everything is fine, which is its own kind of suspicious. Held position. Not every day is a jump. More tomorrow, if the stars stay where I left them.
